sourceLongSummaries: Since leaving Tokra, Kenzo has dreamed nightly of strange landscapes, especially a red sandstone mesa sheltering a clear oasis. He reaches Karawa and finds that exact mesa, temple, oasis, and village before cries for help reveal two enormous hyenas charging into town. In a parallel introduction, Delwath has spent several months lodging above Badya's teahouse, investigating the Temple of Shakun and helping during an earlier hyena attack; his morning is interrupted when villagers call for the elf again.

Kenzo, Delwath, Seeker, and Wellby emerge from different parts of Karawa and see two horse-sized hyenas selecting victims among the fleeing villagers. After the strangers size one another up, a hyena mauls a young villager and the fight begins. Delwath fires a crackling magical blast, Seeker's first crossbow shot goes wide, and Kenzo rushes into melee, landing a rapid sequence of staff and unarmed strikes that badly wounds one beast.

Kenzo repeatedly pounds the first hyena with his staff and fists, endures a vicious bite, and finally kills it. Wellby stabilizes the villager the beasts mauled, while Beli repeatedly tries and fails to call on divine magic. Against the other hyena, Delwath uses crackling blasts and black flame, Seeker distracts it with an illusory baby antelope and then drops its forelegs into an excavated hole, and Wellby exploits its prone position to drive his sword into a weak point and end the fight.

As warnings of more beasts echo through Karawa, the villagers scatter and Beli leaves to get Candrosa. Delwath carries the stabilized man into Badya's teahouse, where Badya agrees to watch him, and then rejoins Kenzo, Wellby, and Seeker beside the hyena corpses. They establish that the beasts entered from the east-northeast and were not simply ordinary animals enlarged by a spell; dried blood on one body suggests the hyenas fought or killed something before reaching Karawa, giving the strangers their first clue to follow.

Kenzo, Wellby, Seeker, and Delwath introduce themselves and compare what drew them to Karawa. Seeker notes dried blood from earlier violence on a hyena and proposes tracking the beasts, while Delwath senses a distortion in the Weave around the scene. Under the teahouse awning, Seeker heals Kenzo and explains that magical lines converge within the mesa and Temple of Shakun; Wellby identifies himself as a mapmaker seeking the blank lands to the east, and the group begins recognizing overlapping interests in Karawa, old Dunmar, and the source of the attack.

Beli returns with Candrosa and Elder Kisa, heals Delwath and Kenzo with red ochre paste, and helps other acolytes carry the wounded villager away. Kisa explains that this is the third recent attack, that the beasts are growing stronger, and that the approaching festival leaves Karawa dangerously exposed; she asks Delwath and the travelers to investigate. When Delwath reports that Beli's divine magic failed and that he sensed a distortion in the Weave resembling the power of ancient elven masters, Candrosa turns pale, acknowledges mysteries he cannot discuss openly, and leaves to check on his acolytes while Kisa entrusts the problem to Delwath.

Delwath asks Kenzo, Wellby, and Seeker to help track the beasts, and all three agree despite their separate interests in Candrosa, the temple, and the lands east of Karawa. During a short preparation interval, Kenzo secures a room, Wellby equips himself for travel, and Seeker inspects the Temple of Shakun from outside, confirming a powerful convergence inside the mesa and sensing an unidentified concentration of valuable stone. Once the group regathers, Delwath and Wellby search the town's outskirts, recover the two hyenas' large claw prints heading east, and prepare to follow them with Delwath's horse and supplies.

sourceShortSummaries: The party follows the hyenas east-northeast until their tracks vanish in rocky badlands, then climbs for a view and chooses a moving dust cloud to the north as its next lead.
The party intercepts Alesh on the old trade road, learns of missing herders and renewed danger around Gomat, and decides to push toward the oasis.
sourceLongSummaries: The group follows the giant claw prints east-northeast through blooming scrub for several hours, but the trail disappears when the terrain becomes bare rock. They continue along the beasts' general heading while discussing whether magic, Shakun, or the realm of dreams might explain the attack, only to become disoriented among twisting slot and box canyons. Wellby uses a grappling hook to climb above the badlands, reestablishes Karawa's direction, spots a much deeper canyon to the east and a moving dust cloud to the north, and the party decides to intercept whatever is raising the dust.

Leaving the canyonlands, the party discovers that the dust belongs to Alesh, a Dunmari scout returning from Gomat. She has seen nothing dangerous on the road itself, but reports missing herders, unsettling rumors among scouts and pastoralists, and fears that the old dangers of the Nashtkar may be returning. The blood on the hyenas and the line of their approach make Gomat the party's best lead; Alesh explains the route, identifies Akan and his family as friendly herders camped there, then rides on toward her own family while the group chooses a hurried journey to the oasis over returning to defend Karawa.

locationRefs: old trade road east of Karawa
sourceShortSummaries: After camping beside the old road, the party force-marches through the following day and reaches Gomat exhausted to find giant lizards feeding among silent tents.
sourceLongSummaries: The party follows the ancient road through land visibly twisted by past cataclysms, camps for a cold and quiet night, and resumes before dawn. They push through a full day of desert heat into the moonlit evening, leaving Kenzo, Wellby, and Seeker exhausted. At Gomat Oasis the tents stand silent and unlit; dead sheep lie near the camp, and three pony-sized lizards tear into the carcasses without yet noticing the party.

sourceEntries.boundaryReason: With the hyenas dead, the villagers scatter for help while the strangers tend the wounded, inspect the bodies, and begin introducing themselves.
sourceEntries.shortSummary: Beli runs to fetch Candrosa while Delwath and Wellby move the rescued villager into Badya's teahouse and the four strangers begin examining the attack.
sourceEntries.longSummary: As warnings of more beasts echo through Karawa, the villagers scatter and Beli leaves to get Candrosa. Delwath carries the stabilized man into Badya's teahouse, where Badya agrees to watch him, and then rejoins Kenzo, Wellby, and Seeker beside the hyena corpses. They establish that the beasts entered from the east-northeast and were not simply ordinary animals enlarged by a spell; dried blood on one body suggests the hyenas fought or killed something before reaching Karawa, giving the strangers their first clue to follow.

recapBlocks.title: Karawa Asks for Help
sourceShortSummaries: Beli heals Delwath and Kenzo before Kisa asks the strangers to investigate the escalating attacks and Candrosa reacts uneasily to the failure of Beli's magic.
sourceLongSummaries: Beli returns with Candrosa and Elder Kisa, heals Delwath and Kenzo with red ochre paste, and helps other acolytes carry the wounded villager away. Kisa explains that this is the third recent attack, that the beasts are growing stronger, and that the approaching festival leaves Karawa dangerously exposed; she asks Delwath and the travelers to investigate. When Delwath reports that Beli's divine magic failed and that he sensed a distortion in the Weave resembling the power of ancient elven masters, Candrosa turns pale, acknowledges mysteries he cannot discuss openly, and leaves to check on his acolytes while Kisa entrusts the problem to Delwath.

recapBlocks.title: Into the Badlands
sourceShortSummaries: Delwath recruits the other three travelers, who rest and prepare before Seeker examines the mesa and the group finds the hyenas' eastbound tracks.
The party follows the hyenas east-northeast until their tracks vanish in rocky badlands, then climbs for a view and chooses a moving dust cloud to the north as its next lead.
sourceLongSummaries: Delwath asks Kenzo, Wellby, and Seeker to help track the beasts, and all three agree despite their separate interests in Candrosa, the temple, and the lands east of Karawa. During a short preparation interval, Kenzo secures a room, Wellby equips himself for travel, and Seeker inspects the Temple of Shakun from outside, confirming a powerful convergence inside the mesa and sensing an unidentified concentration of valuable stone. Once the group regathers, Delwath and Wellby search the town's outskirts, recover the two hyenas' large claw prints heading east, and prepare to follow them with Delwath's horse and supplies.

The group follows the giant claw prints east-northeast through blooming scrub for several hours, but the trail disappears when the terrain becomes bare rock. They continue along the beasts' general heading while discussing whether magic, Shakun, or the realm of dreams might explain the attack, only to become disoriented among twisting slot and box canyons. Wellby uses a grappling hook to climb above the badlands, reestablishes Karawa's direction, spots a much deeper canyon to the east and a moving dust cloud to the north, and the party decides to intercept whatever is raising the dust.

recapBlocks.title: The Road to Gomat
locationRefs: old trade road east of Karawa
sourceShortSummaries: The party intercepts Alesh on the old trade road, learns of missing herders and renewed danger around Gomat, and decides to push toward the oasis.
After camping beside the old road, the party force-marches through the following day and reaches Gomat exhausted to find giant lizards feeding among silent tents.
sourceLongSummaries: Leaving the canyonlands, the party discovers that the dust belongs to Alesh, a Dunmari scout returning from Gomat. She has seen nothing dangerous on the road itself, but reports missing herders, unsettling rumors among scouts and pastoralists, and fears that the old dangers of the Nashtkar may be returning. The blood on the hyenas and the line of their approach make Gomat the party's best lead; Alesh explains the route, identifies Akan and his family as friendly herders camped there, then rides on toward her own family while the group chooses a hurried journey to the oasis over returning to defend Karawa.

The party follows the ancient road through land visibly twisted by past cataclysms, camps for a cold and quiet night, and resumes before dawn. They push through a full day of desert heat into the moonlit evening, leaving Kenzo, Wellby, and Seeker exhausted. At Gomat Oasis the tents stand silent and unlit; dead sheep lie near the camp, and three pony-sized lizards tear into the carcasses without yet noticing the party.
